name: Braciaea

attributes.attribute: equated with Mars by the Romans
name may come from a word for malt

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Braciaea is a god of the continental Celts done in Gaul. The record on him is slight. The people of Rome set him beside their god of war Mars. His name may come from a word for malt. The root lives in Gaulish and Welsh. The root links drink of grain to battle heat. Lords of the Celts gave their soldiers drink before a war.

okr.objective: Describe Braciaea, the Continental Celtic god tied to Mars.
key_results: Braciaea was a god of the Continental Celts.
The Romans equated him with Mars.
His name may derive from a word for malt.
